articles.title: Australia’s Rebecca Henderson claims historic race walk world record
articles.summary: 25-year-old sets new global mark for race walk marathon. Rising star slices 19 seconds off previous record despite rain. Rebecca Henderson walked her way into the history books in Japan by becoming the first Australian track and field athlete in a generation to set a senior world record in a…
body: The rising 25-year-old from Dandenong set a new global mark for the race walk marathon – the sport’s newest championship event – clocking a remarkable three hours 14 minutes 52 seconds at the All Japan Race Walking meeting on Sunday.
What’s more, the Victorian achieved the milestone while having to compete in sodden conditions on a rainy day in Takahata, in northern Japan.

Australian para athletes have broken global records in recent times while Olympic silver medallist Jess Hull also set the world 2000m record a couple of years ago in Monaco in a non-championship discipline.

Yet Henderson’s walk was the first time in 20 years that a non-disabled athlete from the country had set a global mark in an official championship event since another Aussie race walker, Nathan Deakes, set the 50km world record on the roads of Geelong in December 2006.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli looks forward to drivers’ title after victory in US Grand Prix
articles.summary: F1 champion-elect: ‘Hopefully we can clinch it soon’ Italian two points from title but Verstappen unhappy. Kimi Antonelli has acknowledged the Formula One world championship is within his grasp after the Italian took a dominant victory at the US Grand Prix which has put him just two points away…
body: Antonelli beat the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc into second place and the Red Bull of Max Verstappen into third. With his title rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton finishing eighth and fourth respectively, Antonelli will take the title if he finishes ninth or better in Mexico City.

The 20-year-old, who stands to become Formula 1’s youngest champion, was jubilant as he crossed the line at the Circuit of the Americas. “Yeah! That’s how we do it,” he exclaimed to his engineer Peter Bonnington.
“Another small step,” the Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, told Antonelli over the radio after the victory. “Another small step.”

With Mercedes having worked hard to iron out issues with their recent upgrades to the car, the victory was important to the team, who pulled off a coup in opting for a one-stop strategy which paid off handsomely for their world champion-elect driver. Antonelli paid tribute to his team.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli storms to US F1 GP victory but is made to wait for title glory
articles.summary: Championship leader wins from Leclerc and Verstappen. 20-year-old should win title in next race in Mexico. With a calm assurance that belies his tender years, Kimi Antonelli delivered another masterclass at the US Grand Prix, ensuring that while he could not quite seal the Formula One world…
body: Antonelli’s dominant victory in Austin at the Circuit of the Americas, with a controlled and composed drive to beat the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc into second place and the Red Bull of Max Verstappen into third, was described by the Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff as “one small step” towards the title in what has been a season of giant leaps for the Italian.

Those leaps were exemplified by Antonelli’s run in Austin where he did everything required of him, taking pole and converting it to a dominant race win, his ninth of the season. “The race of a champion who isn’t the champion yet,” was Wolff’s accurate assessment.

However, while it was a perfect weekend for the Italian, it was not quite enough to claim the title in Texas. With his teammate George Russell finishing in eighth place and Lewis Hamilton in fourth for Ferrari, the fight remains alive but only just and Antonelli is now in position to finish the job next weekend in Mexico City.

articles.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
articles.summary: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world.
body: “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again.

In the corner, Madrid’s players piled on. This was the Frenchman’s 10th goal against Barcelona but none felt quite like this. Not only was this the first time Barcelona failed to win in the league this season, their record-equalling run halted at nine; it was the first time they had failed to win any game since returning here a year ago.

articles.title: 'The pace was rubbish' - Russell in blunt admission after Austin struggle
articles.summary: George Russell admitted his pace in the United States Grand Prix was "rubbish", with the Mercedes driver at a loss to why he trailed race-winning team-mate Kimi Antonelli by such a large margin,
body: Russell finished 54 seconds behind the sister Mercedes in the 56-lap race in an eighth place that only just kept him in mathematical championship contention heading to next week's race in Mexico, where Antonelli is set to clinch the crown.

Russell had held his grid position of sixth through the race's first stint but dropped to eighth after serving a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop for an incident with Oscar Piastri in the opening lap, when he was judged to have gained an advantage by running off track in battle with the McLaren.
Russell subsequently spent the final 26 laps on the similarly one-stopping Piastri's tail but was unable to find a way back past the Australian driver.
Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The pace was rubbish. That's the long and short of it.

articles.title: Smith holds on to beat Schindler in Euros final
articles.summary: Ross Smith holds off home favourite Martin Schindler to win the European Championship title for a second time, with world champion Luke Littler having been knocked out in the quarter-finals.
body: England's Smith reeled off six legs in a row as he took an 8-2 lead in the best-of-21 final against Germany's Schindler in Dortmund.
Schindler got it back to 9-7 before Smith, who won the tournament in 2022, managed to cross the line for an 11-8 victory.
"It's absolutely amazing," Smith, who beat Luke Woodhouse 10-6 and Gerwyn Price 11-7 to get to the final, told ITV.
"I'm not going to lie, I was a bit sweaty there. He wouldn't let up would he? Full credit to him."

articles.title: Smith beats Schindler in Dortmund thriller after Littler's QF exit
articles.summary: Ross Smith has won the Machineseeker European Championship for a second time after overcoming a late Martin Schindler fightback to claim an 11-8 victory in Dortmund.
body: The 2022 champion fired a 107 average in his last-eight victory over Luke Woodhouse and rallied from 4-1 down to beat Gerwyn Price 11-7, setting up a showdown against German No 1 Schindler at Westfalenhallen.
Smith edged a tight opening session before reeling off six straight legs against Schindler, who almost fell 9-2 behind before capitalising on some wayward finishing to sneak a 20-dart break of throw.

Schindler was broken in the next but offered a four-leg burst - including finishes of 116 and 127 - to cut the deficit to 9-7 and threaten a famous comeback, but the next three legs went with throw as Smith closed out victory and the £150,000 first prize.

Victory sees Smith join Michael van Gerwen, Phil Taylor, Rob Cross and Peter Wright as the only players to win multiple European Championship titles, with his latest success following his World Series of Darts title in September and lifting him to world No 6.

articles.title: Stars 6, Islanders 3: Defensive leaks catch up
articles.summary: The Islanders hung with the Stars in Dallas for two periods, erasing three one-goal deficits before Wyatt Johnston and Jason Robertson pulled the Stars away with two goals in a 5:35 span early in the third period.
body: Matthew Schaefer, Kyle Palmieri and Brayden Schenn got the Islanders goals to tie the game at various points, following frustrating sequences or bad bounces that put the Isles in a hole. They showed defensive cracks all night that the Stars consistently exploited.

The Stars got on the board after the Islanders were buzzing in the Dallas zone and Jake Oettinger was without his stick. That made it sting all the more that Jamie Benn and Tyler Seguin were allowed to counter the other way with a 2-on-1. Seguin shot instead of passing back, and I’m still not sure how his shot found a hole in Ilya Sorokin.

After Schaefer tied it on a rush and neat short-side shot over Oettinger, Schenn coughed up the puck behind the Islanders net to allow Robertson to come around and score point blank for his first of two goals on the night.

And after Kyle Palmieri tied it early in the second on the rebound of a heavy bounce off the end boards, the Stars got a similar bounce to allow Justin Hryckowian to regain the lead, 3-2, on a power play with Logan Stanley in the box.

articles.title: Mbappe's late strike earns Mourinho and Real Clasico glory at Barca
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe's double took Real Madrid to a famous 2-1 Clasico win, which had Jose Mourinho sliding on his knees in celebration in Barcelona.
body: It was the 87th minute when Mbappe tucked in from Eduardo Camavinga's cutback following some sublime skill from Jude Bellingham. The celebrations from Real Madrid were wild, with their head coach unable to contain himself, his staff on the pitch, and his players clashing with Barcelona fans.

Real had been on the defensive after Raphinha's snapshot had levelled a pulsating clash, with Lamine Yamal narrowly clipping wide as LaLiga's defending champions pushed for a winner. Instead Real have closed to within three points of their great rivals. Atletico are second just two off Barca now.

It's been a bad week for Hansi Flick's side, whose 11-game winning streak at the start of this season was halted with defeat in the Champions League at Paris St-Germain. This loss will sting far more - it's Real's first win in Barcelona in three years.

Mbappe's opener had been fortuitous, Gerard Martin slamming a clearance in off him. But Real's move to get to that point had been excellent and throughout the contest they showed they were willing to go toe-to-toe with their more favoured hosts.
